Symmetric scatter correction, the fallback of the additive one

Source: R/imputeCellGLoc.R
dot-gloc_correct_scatter_sym.Rd

The correction that .gloc_correct_scatter applied until VIM 7.5.0, kept as an internal helper for one purpose: .gloc_correct_scatter returns it when a Cholesky factorisation fails during its own iteration. It solves the same diagonal equation but rescales the whole matrix symmetrically, \(\Sigma = D \Sigma_{raw} D\) with \(D = \mathrm{diag}(\kappa_j^{-1/2})\) and the per-column factor \(\kappa_j = 1 - (s_j^2/\sigma_j^2)(1 - \kappa)\), where \(s_j^2 = 1 / (\Sigma^{-1})_{jj}\); \(\kappa_j\) reduces to \(\kappa\) under independence and to 1 when there is no downweighting. It is solved by a fixed-point iteration of at most 50 steps, and if a Cholesky factorisation fails it returns \(\Sigma_{raw} / \kappa\).

.gloc_correct_scatter_sym(S_raw, kappa)

Arguments

S_raw

the uncorrected weighted scatter.

kappa

the scalar consistency factor from .gloc_consistency, \(E[w(Z) Z^2] / E[w(Z)]\) for \(Z \sim N(0, 1)\).

Value

the symmetrically corrected scatter.

Details

It was replaced because it restores the diagonal and multiplies every covariance by \(d_j d_k > 1\), although the weights leave the cross-moments unbiased to first order (see .gloc_correct_scatter). On clean data with five variables at correlation 0.7 and a sixth at 0.1, at n = 20000, the soft corner's block correlation came out at 0.746 and its conditional variances, which detection and the conditional imputation use, at 0.86 of the truth, so clean cells were flagged at 1.8-1.9% against a nominal 1.12%.

Correction, recorded rather than deleted: while this function was .gloc_correct_scatter, its documentation said that the scaling "leaves the correlation matrix alone" and that the correlations "are themselves mildly biased upward by conditional-residual downweighting", a bias "not corrected here". Most of that bias came from the scaling itself: it keeps the correlation matrix of \(\Sigma_{raw}\), whose off-diagonals are close to unbiased while its diagonal is deflated, so the correlations it keeps are too large.
